task.title: Gossipsub reachable mesh and fanout uniqueness
task.requirement: From the actual empty RouterState, every arbitrary finite mixture of the existing Trace.Event receive RPC, heartbeat, join, leave and publish operations preserves unique peers in every mesh and fanout. Require lawful selection only at events that select peers. Derive necessary candidate and peer-table invariants from initialization and actual updates; do not assume the desired property at intermediate states, wrap the router in deduplication, change runtime behavior or weaken the existing seen-cache theorems. Client choices, standing, validation and times may vary per event.
task.next: Review the exact hypotheses and the two mutation controls in .meden/evidence/gossip-reachability.json. On another PC, pull this branch, open the GUI and rerun the local Lean check. Mesh/fanout uniqueness from the actual empty state is proved; network/packet correspondence, liveness and scoring convergence remain separate obligations.

scope: Actual empty RouterState; arbitrary finite Trace.Event mixtures of receive RPC, join, leave, publish and heartbeat. One arbitrary fixed parameter set and message-ID function; client choices, standing, validation and time vary per event. Selection lawfulness is required at heartbeat, join and publish event kinds, with no selection assumption for receive or leave. Peer-table/candidate/fanout invariants are derived through actual operations; no intermediate-state invariant premise or runtime wrapper.
limits: The theorem concerns the pure router and Trace.Event model, not packet/reassembly or real-network correspondence.
It does not establish network liveness, scoring convergence or cryptographic authenticity.
Meden native Rust project verification is separate and remains unaccepted/unverified.
Optional VCVio native crypto backends remain uninstalled and unvalidated.
Stored checks are historical observations; recheck locally after cloning.
